strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear visualization of complementary strengths between VFMs and VLMs through t-SNE analysis
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 11 diverse benchmarks with consistent ~10% average improvement over CLIP baseline
Principled probabilistic approach using optimal transport that is model-agnostic, scalable, and avoids expensive feature concatenation
Thorough ablation studies (Table 2) effectively validating each component's contribution and demonstrating necessity of joint learning
Training-free method with practical applicability in resource-constrained scenarios requiring no fine-tuning or additional annotations
Robust to hyperparameter selection with sensitivity analysis showing stable performance across reasonable ranges (ε, λ)
Clear and generally well-written presentation with good motivation and intuitive explanations of the method
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: applies established optimal transport techniques (Caron et al. 2020) and standard GMM modeling to a new problem setting without significant methodological innovation

Insufficient justification for key design choices: (1) why maximize Tr(Q^T P) + λTr(Q^T Y) rather than minimize a divergence, (2) why shared diagonal covariance is appropriate, (3) why GMM is the right choice for visual distributions

Inadequate evaluation of multiple VFMs: only DINOv2 used in main experiments despite claiming flexibility; Eq. 6 extension presented but not empirically validated; no guidance on setting {ηi}, {λi} weights

Missing critical baselines: no comparison with simple weighted averaging of CLIP and DINOv2 predictions, and no direct quantitative comparison with DINO-assisted prompt learning mentioned as motivation
Limited experimental scope: transductive-only setting prevents assessment of broader applicability; inductive ZSL results absent despite being practically important
No statistical significance testing: single runs reported without error bars or confidence intervals, problematic for potentially small test sets (e.g., Aircraft dataset)
Initialization bias toward semantics: P(0) initialized with semantic distribution Y, undermining claims of symmetric mutual reinforcement between visual and semantic branches
Hyperparameter sensitivity despite 'training-free' claims: performance degrades significantly when λ > 0.7; no principled dataset-agnostic selection strategy provided for new datasets
Missing computational analysis: no runtime comparisons with baselines; no analysis of computational overhead from iterative optimization procedure despite scalability claims

Incomplete investigation of method limitations: modest gains on fine-grained datasets (Aircraft +4.26%) unexplored; no analysis of dataset characteristics determining success; no failure case discussion

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear illustrations of complementary strengths between VLMs (semantic alignment) and VFMs (fine-grained visual features)
Comprehensive experimental validation across 26 benchmarks spanning natural images, medical pathology, and remote sensing domains with consistent improvements
Training-free and prior-free framework applicable to black-box models, eliminating need for fine-tuning or manual weight selection
Thorough ablation studies (Fig. 4, Table 5) systematically demonstrating the importance of each component (VFM introduction, self-adaptive weighting, joint learning)
Practical efficiency: rapid convergence (5-10 iterations), competitive computational overhead, sample-wise inference
Clear presentation with detailed methodology and reproducibility-supporting implementation details in appendix
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: optimal transport application rather than methodological innovation; squared Frobenius form (Eq. 7) is minor modification; MM algorithm is standard practice

Unfair experimental comparisons: SOTA uses multiple models (e.g., CLIP-1+DINOv3) vs. single-model baselines; improvement conflates model quality with fusion benefits; missing simple ensemble baselines (averaging, weighted averaging)

Self-adaptive weighting mechanism lacks theoretical justification: no principled explanation for why lower transport cost implies higher model reliability; post-hoc justification in 6.2 rather than upfront motivation

GMM fitting for high-dimensional VFM features inadequately addressed: no analysis of sample complexity for covariance estimation, K selection unspecified, diagonal covariance assumption introduced late; marginal improvement (+0.3-0.8%) from joint learning (Eq. 8) questions its necessity

Limited generalizability: transductive setting requires unlabeled test data (impractical constraint); inductive setting (Table 4) shows only comparable performance to DMN/COSMIC, not consistent superiority

Experimental rigor concerns: no error bars or significance tests; single-run results; unexplained performance degradation on Aircraft (-2.1%); hyperparameter sensitivity (τ, ϵ, K, initialization) not analyzed

Lack of theoretical grounding: connection between minimizing transport cost and classification accuracy assumed not derived; convergence to stationary points may trap in local minima; no analysis of method success/failure conditions
